subject: Arcturus MAP: benchmark scope, SLOs, and close timeline
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@arcturus.health>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@arcturus.health>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Arcturus MAP - benchmarking scope for initial pilot

Hi Irene / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Arcturus is excited to move the pilot into the MAP phase. Attached is our current workload profile (lightly redacted) — primary ask: validate the performance posture (latency and concurrency) for our main inference flows so we can greenlight the production rollout.

High-level goals we want covered in the MAP benchmarking section:
- Baseline cold start TTFT for single-request interactive flows (voice transcription post-process)
- 95th/99th percentile latency for 2k token generative prompts used by our triage assistant
- Sustained throughput for batched batch-export jobs (nightly analytics)
- Concurrency behavior when multiple interactive users and background batching run together

Proposed timeline: scope confirmation this week, benchmark runs next week, acceptance decision by 4/30 so procurement can finish PO/contract.

Can you confirm the acceptance criteria you'll use (SLOs, pass/fail gates) and any additional sample prompts / traffic patterns you need? I attached arcturus_workload_profile.xlsx and a short sample of QA prompts in arcturus_qa_samples.json.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

— Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering
Arcturus Health

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@arcturus.health>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@arcturus.health>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arcturus MAP - benchmarking scope for initial pilot

Elena — thanks for the profile and the samples. Attaching our initial benchmarking plan (rwd_map_bench_plan_v1.xlsx) with the proposed workload slices and acceptance gates. High-level notes inline below.

TL;DR: We can validate the three flows you called out within your timeline if we run parallel test windows and you give us the confirm on the canonical prompt sets by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed workload slices (short):
- Interactive (live): 1:1 single-turn prompts, 90% short (<256 tokens), 10% long (1k-2k). Peak concurrency target: 120 concurrent users (estimated).
- Long-form generation: 2–4k token outputs, avg token output size 1.6k, throughput target 20 qps sustained when running in isolation.
- Batch export (analytics): batched inputs of 256 requests per batch, throughput target 400 qps for background window.

Pre-test setup and constraints:
- We'll run a cold-cache pass then 3 warm-cache steady windows to capture KV cache behavior.
- Recommend we configure prefix/KV cache to mimic your production prefix-reuse (~30% reuse).
- Quantization/profile: we'll test with FP16 baseline, then 8-bit quantized variant for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Draft acceptance criteria (examples included in spreadsheet):
- TTFT (cold): median < 3.0s, 95th < 6.0s for interactive single requests (on the chosen hardware profile).
- Interactive 95th latency (warm): < 400ms for short prompts, < 1.2s for long prompts.
- Throughput: long-form sustained throughput >= 18 qps in isolation with p95 latency under 2.5s per token generation window.
- Batch job throughput: sustain 350 qps for 5-minute window with <1% error rate.
- Concurrency resilience: when interactive (peak) and batch export run simultaneously, degrade gracefully with no more than 20% increase in p95 latency for interactive flow.

Questions for you:
1) Can you confirm the canonical short and long prompt sets we should run (we've included placeholders in the Drive link)?
2) Any hard SLOs we must guarantee for the contract (e.g., max acceptable p99 latency)?

If that reads OK I'll schedule the runs for next Tue/Wed (4/20–4/21) and post results + a short executive summary.

Best,
Irene
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@arcturus.health>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arcturus MAP - benchmarking scope for initial pilot

Elena / team — a few technical clarifications and the pass/fail gates I want on the run so the MAP's performance section is unambiguous.

On Mon, Apr 18, 2027 at 10:02 AM irene_choi@redwood.ai wrote:
> Draft acceptance criteria (examples included in spreadsheet):
> - TTFT (cold): median < 3.0s, 95th < 6.0s for interactive single requests (on the chosen hardware profile).
> - Interactive 95th latency (warm): < 400ms for short prompts, < 1.2s for long prompts.
> - Throughput: long-form sustained throughput >= 18 qps in isolation with p95 latency under 2.5s per token generation window.
> - Batch job throughput: sustain 350 qps for 5-minute window with <1% error rate.

Proposed concrete test gates (we'll record measured metric and gate pass/fail):
- Gate A (Cold TTFT): cold-run median TTFT <= 3.0s AND max TTFT <= 6.5s across 3 cold starts — otherwise fail.
- Gate B (Warm latency): interactive p95 (short prompt) <= 400ms AND p99 <= 1.0s.
- Gate C (Sustained throughput): long-form throughput >= 18 qps for a 10-minute window with p95 latency <= 2.5s.
- Gate D (Concurrency resilience): when interactive at peak concurrency (120) + batch export at 350 qps, interactive p95 increases <= 20% vs isolated baseline.
- Gate E (Errors): total request error rate < 1% across all runs.

Test harness notes:
- We'll use the Redwood workload generator scheduled in the MAP plan and export raw traces + per-token latencies.
- We'll seed a KV cache layer to mimic 30% prefix reuse and measure cache hit ratio — target hit ratio >= 25% for warm windows.
- We'll run both FP16 and 8-bit quantized variants. If quantized fails gates, we report delta in cost and latency and recommend fallback routing.

If Arcturus confirms Gate B's p99 hard maximum and any procurement-level SLOs, we'll lock the plan. Also please confirm the hardware profile (A100x2 or T4 cluster) you want us to run against; A100x2 recommended for realistic production equivalence.

— Jonas
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@arcturus.health>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@arcturus.health>, procurement@arcturus.health
Date: 2027-04-18T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arcturus MAP - benchmarking scope for initial pilot

Thanks — this looks actionable and clean. Quick responses:
1) We confirm the short/long prompt canonical sets in the Drive folder (I updated the file arcturus_prompts_v2.json).
2) Procurement: target PO by 4/30; if performance gates pass we will proceed with the standard Redwood contract and a 12-month commitment.
3) Hardware: please run the baseline on A100x2; we will also want a T4 run for cost-comparison (non-blocking).
4) Hard SLO ask: please treat interactive p99 <= 1.2s as procurement-level must-have.

We accept the Gate A–E definitions above. Please proceed with the runs on Tue/Wed; I'll be available to review the executive summary and decision matrix right after the runs. DocuSign link for the order is here: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/arcturus-deal-DEAL-AC-2197

On the timeline: procurement will begin drafting the PO on 4/21 assuming a positive preliminary read — we need the executive summary by 4/22 EOD to keep the 4/30 PO cadence.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to results.

— Elena
Head of Platform Engineering, Arcturus Health
